analysis.assetRisk: None. Overflow causes a clean revert with no fund loss or locking.
analysis.attackPath: No attack path exists. The overflow is an eventual mathematical consequence of owner-configured compound growth, not an exploitable vulnerability.
analysis.conditions: Requires thousands of mints at typical growth rates. By the time overflow occurs, price already exceeds total supply of any token -- minting is already economically impossible.
analysis.impact: Zero additional impact. The overflow merely changes the revert reason from 'insufficient balance' to 'arithmetic overflow'. The functional outcome is identical.

severityAudit.disagreementReason: The overflow does not independently impact protocol availability. Minting is already impossible due to astronomically high prices long before overflow occurs. No funds are at risk. Owner can trivially recover via setPrice(). This is a mathematical observation about the endpoint of an exponential curve, not a protocol vulnerability. Per C4 criteria, this is QA/Low: a state-handling observation with no security impact.
severityAudit.overlapWithExistingFindings: C-01 already covers the root cause: uncapped growthBasisPoints allowing owner to make minting prohibitively expensive. ECON-007 describes a redundant downstream symptom.

mathVerification.case1_1pct_growth: At 1% growth from 1 token: price exceeds total supply of most tokens after ~2000-3000 mints. Overflow at ~4200 mints when price is ~1e38 tokens.
mathVerification.case2_10pct_growth: At 10% growth from 1 token: price exceeds all conceivable holdings within ~200 mints. Overflow at ~420 mints when price is ~1e35 tokens.
mathVerification.case3_extreme_growth: At 500% growth: price exceeds 2 billion tokens after just 12 mints. Overflow at ~76 mints.
mathVerification.conclusion: Economic DoS precedes arithmetic DoS by orders of magnitude in all cases.

severityAudit.notes: Recommend downgrade to Low/QA. The finding is technically accurate but the severity claim is overstated. The overflow is a theoretical curiosity, not a practical vulnerability. It adds no impact beyond what the exponential pricing curve already guarantees.
